request.prompt:
VIEW 3 — THE SAME MAP SEEN FROM THE WEST, A LOW SIDE ELEVATION ACROSS ITS WHOLE LENGTH. The same place, the same hand and the same moonlit night as the first image.

ONE single full-frame wide view. Not a grid, not panels, not insets. No text, no labels, no interface.

The eye stands far out on the open sea to the west, a few blocks above the water, looking east, so the whole map is seen side-on from end to end, north on the LEFT and south on the RIGHT.
- Left: the town of Wrackham climbing its cliff in terraces, from a stone harbour wall at the waterline (about four blocks above the sea) up to the coach road at the cliff top about thirty blocks higher; tall grey stone houses with steep slate roofs and a few lit windows, a small chapel bell tower, and the round lighthouse at the end of the breakwater standing out over the water.
- Centre, the longest part of the frame: the flat — a low, level plain of wet black mud only two blocks above the sea, stretching far to the right, with a faint line of marker stakes along it, wrecked hulls lying on their sides, the mast of a grounded launch, a few standing stone pillars.
- Right of centre: a gap of open black sea water where the mud ends, with a small stone ferry house on each side of it.
- Right: the creature on its own low bank of mud — a hill-sized whale-like leviathan built of dark blocks, about 45 blocks high at its back, head to the left facing the town, mouth low at the front of the head, a carved pale stone slab set in its forehead, a ridged spine falling away to the tail on the right; its left-facing flank shows three dark torn wounds.
- The full moon high in the sky over the creature; open ocean to the horizon behind everything.
request.style_note: The Stranding: every image in this series is one place drawn in the same hand — a Minecraft Java Edition build shown as a high-quality in-game screenshot with a soft night shader. Every surface is made of visible one-metre cubic blocks with vanilla Minecraft textures (cobblestone, stone bricks, spruce and dark oak planks and logs, deepslate, mud and packed mud, black and grey concrete, prismarine, lanterns, glass panes), crisp block edges, no smooth curves anywhere: round or organic forms are stepped block shapes. The place is a grey slate-roofed fishing town on cliff terraces above a bay, a plain of wet black mud risen from the bay, and a vast stranded sea creature built of dark blocks lying at the far edge of the mud. Night under a clear sky and a bright full moon: cold blue-silver moonlight on wet mud and slate roofs, deep blue-black shadows, small warm yellow pools of lantern light at doors and windows, sea water near-black with silver moon glints. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset, never a caption, no text, no labels, no border, no interface.
